summary: Updates RFC 5575 to clarify the format of the BGP Flowspec Redirect Extended Community. It was replaced by RFC 8955.

eli5.summary: A confusing line in the rulebook is cleared up. It was later replaced by RFC 8955.

questions: what is the flowspec redirect extended community
how is the bgp flowspec redirect formatted
what are the three flowspec redirect formats
subtitle: Clarifies how BGP Flowspec redirects traffic using Route Target formats.

tldr.problem: RFC 5575 defined a BGP Flowspec Redirect Extended Community that tells routers to send matching traffic to a specific VRF, but did not clearly specify what format the embedded Route Target should use, causing implementations to differ.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines three distinct Redirect Extended Communities, one for each Route Target format (2-octet AS, 4-octet IPv4 address, 4-octet AS), using different IANA codepoints (0x8008, 0x8108, 0x8208) so routers can match the correct VRF.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7674 was replaced by RFC 8955, which consolidates and updates Flowspec specifications.

today: RFC 7674 was replaced by RFC 8955, which updates BGP Flowspec specifications to version 2.

sections.title: The Flowspec Redirect Problem
sections.content:
BGP Flowspec (RFC 5575) lets routers filter and redirect traffic based on packet contents. A Redirect Extended Community tells a router to send matching traffic to the VRF that lists a specific Route Target in its import policy.

The problem: RFC 5575 documented the Redirect as a '6-byte Route Target' but did not specify which format of Route Target to use. Different vendors implemented this ambiguity differently. Some routers tried to match the Route Target value while ignoring its format, causing redirects to go to the wrong VRF.
sections.eli5: The original rule said to redirect based on a Route Target, but did not say which kind of Route Target. Different companies interpreted it differently, causing confusion.

sections.title: Three Redirect Formats
sections.content:
Route Targets come in three formats, distinguished by their IANA type code:

Type 0x8008 (AS-2byte): Uses a 2-octet Autonomous System number and a 4-octet value. Written as 65000:100 (AS number, then value).

Type 0x8108 (IPv4): Uses a 4-octet IPv4 address and a 2-octet value. Written as 192.0.2.1:100 (IPv4 address, then value).

Type 0x8208 (AS-4byte): Uses a 4-octet Autonomous System number and a 2-octet value. Written as 65000.0:100 (4-octet AS number, then value).

This RFC clarifies that the Flowspec Redirect Extended Community uses the same format as the Route Target it contains. A router receiving a Redirect must match not just the Route Target value, but also its format, ensuring traffic goes to the correct VRF.
sections.eli5: Route Targets use different formats. The redirect now says which format is inside, so routers pick the right VRF.

sections.title: IANA Registry Updates
sections.content:
The RFC updates the IANA BGP Extended Communities registries to clarify the codepoint assignments. The original type 0x8008 (Redirect AS-2byte) is clarified in the Generic Transitive Experimental Use registry. Two new registries are created:

Part 2 (type 0x81): For sub-types using 4-octet IPv4 address format, adding Redirect IPv4 (sub-type 0x08).

Part 3 (type 0x82): For sub-types using 4-octet AS format, adding Redirect AS-4byte (sub-type 0x08).

This structure allows implementations to detect the format from the type byte alone, eliminating the ambiguity.
sections.eli5: The registry now lists three different codepoints, one for each Route Target format, so routers know which format is being used.

sections.title: Security Impact of Clarity
sections.content:
The ambiguity in the original RFC 5575 could cause a router to redirect traffic to the wrong VRF if it used 'value wildcard' matching instead of format-aware matching. This misrouting could affect connectivity or security policies.

By clarifying that each Route Target format has its own distinct Redirect Extended Community codepoint, this RFC ensures routers cannot accidentally match the wrong VRF. Operators who have configured Flowspec rules with Route Targets should verify that their routers use the correct format-specific codepoint to avoid unintended traffic misdirection.
sections.eli5: The clarity fixes a problem where traffic could go to the wrong place. Now routers have to be explicit about which format they use, preventing accidents.
